name: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (PV / ET / myelofibrosis)
theme: the JAK era · the count-control discipline

meta.title: Myeloproliferative neoplasms in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: BCR::ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms (polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, myelofibrosis), adult
meta.population: Adults with the classic BCR::ABL1-negative MPNs - ONE spec, two archetype branches, per the granularity check the catalog requested: PV and ET share the COUNT-CONTROL branch (risk-stratify, aspirin, cytoreduce, escalate - diseases managed in decades where the enemy is the clot), and myelofibrosis is the JAK-AND-TRANSPLANT branch (inhibitor selection by cytopenia phenotype; transplant the only cure). The split was declined because the driver-mutation spine (JAK2 V617F, CALR, MPL, triple-negative), the progression pathways (PV/ET -> secondary MF -> blast phase), and the guideline packaging (NCCN and PDQ each cover the family in one document) are shared. BCR::ABL1-positive disease reroutes to the LIVE CML trainer; MDS and the MDS/MPN overlaps to the live MDS trainer's territory; mastocytosis and eosinophilic disorders have their own rows.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the diseases managed in decades. The count-control branch runs on receipts old enough to vote and precise enough to teach: CYTO-PV made 45% a rule (HCT <45% vs 45-50%: cardiovascular death or major thrombosis 2.7% vs 9.8%, HR 3.91), ECLAP made aspirin near-universal in PV (wrong-PMID catch #24 lives on that citation - the memory-candidate was wrong and the live match caught it), revised IPSET-thrombosis routes ET (where CALR-mutant disease clots at roughly half the JAK2 rate), and PT1 versus ANAHYDRET is taught as the honest tension it is. The MF branc…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022) with the ICC (2022) as the concordant parallel naming (differences matter more in MDS/AML); revised IPSET-thrombosis for ET; DIPSS/MIPSS70 for MF (MYSEC-PM for post-PV/ET MF - the score changes with the history); NCCN MPN v2.2026 (secondhand - 403)
meta.response: Count control is the standing response read in PV/ET (HCT <45% - the 45% rule; platelet and WBC control); in MF the trial currencies are SVR35 (spleen volume) and TSS50 (symptoms) - and the field's recurring lesson is that they can split

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Age >60 is itself a risk criterion in PV and ET (it moves the cytoreduction line) and a transplant-eligibility axis in MF.
Patient.helpPatient: In these diseases age is part of the formal risk score, not just background.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Mostly a transplant-fitness and trial-eligibility axis here - the count-control branch rarely turns on it.
Patient.helpPatient: Overall strength matters most for the transplant conversation.

Disease.label: Which MPN
Disease.help: BCR::ABL1 testing is obligatory: a positive is CML (its trainer is LIVE - the gate links it); MDS and the MDS/MPN overlaps belong with the live MDS trainer's biology; mastocytosis/eosinophilic disord…
Disease.helpPatient: Several related blood conditions share this family - the exact diagnosis picks the playbook, and one relative (CML) already has its own page here.

Disease.label: Driver mutation
Disease.help: Diagnostic spine and prognostic input at once: revised IPSET counts JAK2 as a thrombosis point, and CALR-mutant ET clots at roughly half the JAK2 rate (Rumi) - the same platelet count, different risk.
Disease.helpPatient: Which gene drives the disease shapes the clot risk - two people with identical counts can carry different risks.

Count-control routing.label: Thrombosis risk (PV/ET branch)
Count-control routing.help: The count-control branch's routing bit: high-risk (age >60 and/or prior thrombosis; revised IPSET adds the JAK2 point in ET) moves cytoreduction from optional to standard.
Count-control routing.helpPatient: Age and any past clot decide whether count-lowering medicine joins the daily aspirin.

MF routing.label: MF cytopenia phenotype (the niche map)
MF routing.help: The MF branch's signature: four approved JAK inhibitors sorted by the patient's counts - the CBC routes the drug. Momelotinib's ACVR1 co-inhibition is why anemia improves on it; pacritinib holds the…
MF routing.helpPatient: For the scarring form, which blood count is lowest picks which of four similar drugs fits best.

MF routing.label: Transplant eligibility (MF)
MF routing.help: MIPSS70 was built for exactly this call in transplant-age patients: alloHCT is the only potentially curative MF therapy, offered at int-2/high risk - and the window is real (the disease and its cytop…
MF routing.helpPatient: A donor transplant is the one treatment that can cure the scarring form - a genuine conversation for some, with honest timing pressure.

On treatment.label: Count control (the standing read)
On treatment.help: The registry's slowest checkpoint: in PV the target is numeric and trial-proven (HCT <45% - CYTO-PV's 2.7% vs 9.8% events); loss of control escalates the ladder, and phenotype DRIFT (falling counts,…
On treatment.helpPatient: Routine blood counts are the whole scoreboard - in range means the plan is working; drifting means the plan (or the diagnosis) gets re-read.

Newly diagnosed.name: Phlebotomy to <45% + aspirin (the 45% rule - PV's foundation)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the universal PV foundation (NCCN v2.2026 secondhand; PDQ live)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (CYTO-PV target; ECLAP aspirin) - the branch's old, exact receipts
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: needle appointments and intended iron deficiency (fatigue is discussed, not dismissed) - the lightest ledger in the registry
Newly diagnosed.patient: For PV: regular blood draws keeping the thickness below a trial-proven line (45%), plus a daily baby aspirin - managed this way, the disease is usually lived with for decades.

Newly diagnosed.name: Cytoreduction for high-risk PV (HU / ropeginterferon; ruxolitinib on resistance)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: high-risk standard (age >60 and/or prior thrombosis) - NCCN secondhand
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: HU's cytopenias and ulcers vs interferon's flu-and-mood ledger - a real choice, often made by age and pregnancy plans
Newly diagnosed.patient: For higher-risk PV (over 60, or a past clot): a count-lowering medicine joins the draws and aspirin - two proven choices with different personalities, and a third if the first fails.

Newly diagnosed.name: Risk-adapted ET therapy (revised IPSET routes it; PT1 anchors it)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: revised IPSET-routed (NCCN secondhand); PT1 the high-risk anchor
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized (PT1, ANAHYDRET - the honest pair) + validated risk models
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: often none beyond aspirin; HU's ledger where risk earns it - the branch's quietest card
Newly diagnosed.patient: For ET: a formal risk score - past clots, age, and which gene - decides between watching, aspirin alone, or adding a count-lowering pill. Many people need almost nothing for years.
drugs: Aspirin by tier +/- hydroxyurea (anagrelide the taught alternative)

Newly diagnosed.name: JAK inhibitor by phenotype (the niche map - COMFORT / JAKARTA / PERSIST-2 / MOMENTUM)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: four approved JAK inhibitors, niche-sorted (NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x4 (COMFORT-I/II, JAKARTA, PERSIST-2, MOMENTUM) - each owning its lane; OS crossover-honesty carried
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cytopenias by agent (the map exists because they differ), fedratinib's thiamine discipline, momelotinib's gentler anemia profile
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the scarring form: four related pills, chosen by which of YOUR counts is lowest - they shrink the spleen and quiet the symptoms, and picking the right lane is most of the skill.
drugs: Ruxolitinib / fedratinib / pacritinib / momelotinib - by counts

Newly diagnosed.name: Allogeneic transplant (the only cure - for the eligible, in the window)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: registry/consensus (no RCT exists or will) - the estimate flagged, the only-cure framing solid
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the transplant's full ledger (conditioning, GVHD, infections) - the one card here that buys cure with real early risk
Newly diagnosed.patient: For higher-risk scarring disease in fit patients with a donor: the transplant is the one road that can cure - bought with a genuinely hard first year, and best discussed early because the option does not wait forever.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; transfusion rhythm and spleen symptoms are the craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining disease-directed treatment is a real choice - in the slower forms it overlaps with simple watching; in the scarring form it centers on comfort, energy, and transfusions.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: The JAK switch (same map, re-read by today's counts)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: phenotype-routed switching (NCCN secondhand); the pending shelf dated, not carded
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: randomized per-lane evidence (JAKARTA/PERSIST-2/MOMENTUM); the post-JAK median itself flagged
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: each lane's ledger, now with the window watch sharper - post-JAK MF is where the transplant and trial conversations stop being optional
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When the first pill stops working: the same four-drug map, re-read with today's counts - and an honest shelf of promising drugs that are real but not yet approved, each labeled with exactly where it stands.
drugs: Fedratinib / pacritinib / momelotinib - by today's counts

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Transplant (the window, revisited under pressure)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the only cure, under a narrowing window (NCCN secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: registry/consensus - flagged estimate; the framing solid
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the transplant ledger with less reserve than the upfront version - said plainly
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The cure conversation, now under time pressure: still real for fit patients with donors, and harder-won than it would have been earlier - which is why this trainer talks about the window from day one.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort in advanced disease is a real road - built around energy, transfusions, and good days.

milestones.title: Which MPN + thrombosis risk
review: WHICH MPN (PV / ET / MF) + driver mutation (JAK2 / CALR / MPL) - CALR-ET has HALF the thrombosis risk (firsthand); JAK2-ET sits on the PV spectrum
PV: Hct <45% is randomized fact (CYTO-PV 2.7-vs-9.8%) + aspirin (ECLAP RR 0.40) - the floor everyone gets
ET: revised IPSET-thrombosis routes cytoreduction; the PT-1-vs-ANAHYDRET tension is carried, not resolved
MF: MIPSS70 12-fold survival spread routes transplant; JAK choice by cytopenia phenotype (platelets -> pacritinib, anemia -> momelotinib)

IMpactMF: imetelstat vs best available therapy (the OS-primary trial - window closing)
Shorespan-006: bomedemstat vs best available therapy (HU-inadequate ET)

JAK2 vs CALR mutation status in ET: substantially different course - JAK2-mutant ET thrombosis approaches PV rates and runs roughly 2x CALR-mutant disease; CALR: higher platelets, lower Hb/WBC. CROSSOVER HONESTY on the pooled OS (Haematologica 2015, PMID 26069290, matched; long-term PMID 27211272, matched): the survival benefit is crossover-confounded/exploratory, not a clean ITT win - carried as such. Pardanani et al. JAKARTA (NCT01437787), fedratinib in JAK-inhibitor-NAIVE intermediate-2/high-risk MF, re-read firsthand 2026-09-10: spleen response at week 24 was 36% (35 of 96, 95% CI 27-46) at 400 mg and 40% (39 of 97, 30-50) at 500 mg versus 1% (1 of 96, 0-3) on placebo; symptom response was 36% (33 of 91, 26-46) and 34% (31 of 91, 24-44) versus 7% (6 of 85, 2-13). The previously displayed 'SVR 47% / symptoms 40% vs 1% / 9%' matches none of those columns and has been replaced; the Wernicke/thiamine monitoring history carried (none at 400 mg in the updated analysis, PMID 34331348, matched). JAMA Oncol 2015 (PMID 26181658, pubmed-url-match) | PMID 26181658 + abstract read firsthand 2026-08-26

THE SPLEEN-SYMPTOM SPLIT (the field-wide pattern, 2024-2026): three consecutive 1L MF combination phase 3s met the SVR35 co-primary and MISSED the symptom co-primary - MANIFEST-2 pelabresib (66% vs 35%; Nat Med 2025-03; transformation-imbalance flag; NOT filed in the US), TRANSFORM-1 navitoclax (spleen doubled, symptoms missed, fate uncertain), SENTRY selinexor (49.8% vs 28.0%, symptoms missed; JCO 2026-06; sNDA filing imminent as of 2026-08). A shrinking spleen is not a better day - all statuses secondhand, dated 2026-08-19, none approved

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

GIV-IN PV (NCT06093672): givinostat vs hydroxyurea, high-risk JAK2+ PV, 1L cytoreduction, phase 3, composite week-48 response primary (~220 pts; fast-tracked 2026-02) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (ASH 12/2025 TPS + news 2026-02), NOT registry-loaded - re-check due. VERIFY complete (PDUFA Q3 2026) and SANRECO positive-awaiting-phase-3: named, not open

POIESIS (NCT06479135): navtemadlin (MDM2i) add-on for suboptimal ruxolitinib response, JAKi-naive MF entering run-in, TP53 WILD-TYPE required, phase 3 double-blind, SVR35-wk24 primary - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08; primary completion listed 2026-12 - ENROLLMENT WINDOW CLOSING, urgent re-check

MANIFEST-3 (NCT07357727): pelabresib + ruxolitinib vs placebo + ruxolitinib, JAKi-naive MF (DIPSS int-1+; spleen >=450 cm3), phase 3, Novartis, started 2026-06 - CONFLICTING CACHED STATUSES (not-yet-recruiting vs US sites open): the sweep's loudest re-check flag; treat as opening

IMpactMF (NCT04576156): imetelstat vs best available therapy, JAKi-relapsed/refractory int-2/high MF - the ONLY OS-PRIMARY phase 3 in MF; ~80% enrolled (172 sites), interim expected 2H2026 - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08; may close imminently - HIGHEST-PRIORITY re-check. Imetelstat is approved only in lower-risk MDS anemia, NOT MF

RALLY-MF (NCT05320198): DISC-0974 (anti-hemojuvelin, hepcidin-suppressing) for MF/MDS anemia, cohorted by transfusion status, JAKi allowed, phase 1b/2 (55% major hematologic response, ASCO 2026) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache 2026-01), re-check due. INDEPENDENCE luspatercept MISSED its primary - named, not a door

Shorespan-006 (NCT06079879): bomedemstat (LSD1i) vs best available therapy, ET with HU-inadequate response/intolerance, phase 3, durable clinicohematologic response primary (~300 pts, Merck) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08, re-check due; 1L sibling Shorespan-007 (NCT06456346, vs HU, cytoreduction-naive) also recruits
